acceptance_behavior: Through the command path run(argv) with --approval-id, --preflight and an --out path that reaches a temporary repository root through a real symlinked alias of an ancestor directory, the command returns 0 and reports status ok; before the fix it raised ApprovalRejected approval_output_outside_repository

The destination returned by _contained_destination for that alias path can be used exactly as run() uses it: destination.relative_to(root), where root is the resolved repository root passed in, succeeds and gives the repository-relative POSIX path (for example sub/out.json); returning the unresolved alias path is not acceptable because run() would then raise ValueError in the issuance and --recover-output paths

A destination whose parent truly resolves outside the repository is still rejected with approval_output_outside_repository, both for a plain outside path and for a path through a symlink inside the repository that points outside, and both through run(argv) --preflight and the helper
A destination whose final path component is a symlink (inside the repository) is still rejected with approval_output_invalid by the helper
A relative --out path still resolves against the repository root and is accepted when inside it, and its returned destination relates to the root via relative_to
The behavior without --approval-id (the legacy path) is unchanged
intent.objective: Make agentctl approve accept an --out path that reaches the repository through a symlinked alias of an ancestor directory, end to end through the command path (replan of DEMO-001 after a blocking review). KNOWN REVIEW FINDING from an earlier attempt at this fix (task DEMO-001, independent reviewer, blocking): the earlier candidate only removed the lexical check `destination.relative_to(root)` from _contained_destination. That makes the helper ACCEPT an alias path, but it still RETURNS the path unresolved (candidate.absolute()). The caller run() in approve.py then executes `destination.relative_to(config.repo_root)` on that return value, in the approval-issuance path (register(record, path=...)) and in the --recover-output path (the final print, after _write_exclusive_json already created the file). PurePath.relative_to is purely lexical, so an alias path such as <base>/alias-repo/sub/out.json is not relative to <base>/real-repo and raises an uncaught ValueError: the command crashes, after the human has authenticated, for exactly the input the fix is meant to support (and --preflight reports ok for a path the real run cannot finish). The earlier test only re-applied .parent.resolve() to the helper's return value, so it passed while the command was broken. A correct fix must return the contained destination in a form run() accepts, for example destination.parent.resolve(strict=False) / destination.name, with the final-component symlink check still applied, and its tests must exercise the caller-level behavior, not only the helper's resolved parent.
